Which of the following are the example of double salt?

(A) ${\mathrm{FeSO}}_{4} \cdot {\left({\mathrm{NH}}_{4}\right)}_{2}{\mathrm{SO}}_{4} \cdot 6{H}_{2}O$

(B) ${\mathrm{CuSO}}_{4} \cdot 4{\mathrm{NH}}_{3} \cdot {H}_{2}O$

Ammonia solution in water gives a blue precipitate when it combines with a solution of copper salt. The pale blue precipitate of copper hydroxide dissolves in excess of ammonium hydroxide forming tetraamine copper[II] sulphate, an azure blue (deep blue) soluble complex salt.

(C) ${K}_{2}{\mathrm{SO}}_{4} \cdot {\mathrm{Al}}_{2}{\left({\mathrm{SO}}_{4}\right)}_{3} \cdot 24{H}_{2}O$ (Potash alum)

It is a double salt. Basically, it is comprised of two simple salts potassium sulphate and aluminium sulphate. Potash alum will not be wet in its solid form because the water of crystallisation is not free.

(D) $\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}{)}_{2} \cdot 4\mathrm{KCN}$

It is complex salt. It does not dissociate completely into individual ions.

So, the correct answer is A and C only.

questions.question:
The correct statements among I to III are:

(I) Valence bond theory cannot explain the color exhibited by transition metal complexes.

(II) Valence bond theory can predict quantitatively the magnetic properties of transition metal complexes.

(III) Valence bond theory cannot distinguish ligands as weak and strong field ones.
questions.explanation:
Valence Bond Theory (VBT) has several limitations in explaining the properties of coordination compounds.

Statement (I) is correct. VBT does not explain the optical properties or the color exhibited by transition metal complexes. The color is primarily due to d-d electron transitions, which are successfully explained by Crystal Field Theory (CFT).

Statement (II) is incorrect. VBT only provides a qualitative idea about the magnetic properties, such as whether a complex is paramagnetic or diamagnetic based on the presence of unpaired electrons. It cannot predict magnetic properties quantitatively.

Statement (III) is correct. VBT does not distinguish between weak field and strong field ligands. It relies on experimentally observed magnetic moments to assume whether inner or outer d-orbitals are used for hybridization, without explaining why certain ligands cause electron pairing while others do not. The classification of ligands into weak and strong fields is a feature of CFT.

Therefore, only statements (I) and (III) are correct.

Octahedral complexes of copper $\left(\mathrm{II}\right)$ undergo structural distortion (Jahn-Teller). Which one of the given copper $\left(\mathrm{II}\right)$ complexes will show the maximum structural distortion?

(en-ethylenediamine; ${H}_{2}N - {\mathrm{CH}}_{2} - {\mathrm{CH}}_{2} - {\mathrm{NH}}_{2}$)
questions.explanation:
According to John teller any nonlinear molecular system in a degenerate electronic state will be unstable and will undergo some kind of distortion which will lower its symmetry and energy and split the degenerate state. In case of octahedral d9 configuration, the last electron may occupy either $dz^{2}$ or ${\mathrm{dx}}^{2} - {y}^{2}$orbitals of eg set. If it occupies $dz^{2}$ orbital most of the electron density will be concentrated between the metal and the two ligands on the z axis. Thus there will be greater electrostatic repulsion associated with these ligands than with the other four on xy plane. The Jahn Teller effect is mostly observed in octahedral environments. The considerable distortions are usually observed in high spin $d^{4}$, low spin $d^{7}$ and $d^{9}$ configuration

There is unsymmetrical filling of ${e}_{g}$ subset of ${\mathrm{Cu}}^{ + 2}$ ion, while there is symmetrical distribution in ${t}_{2g}$ set, if the complex has same ligand there will be equal repulsion which leads to symmetrical bond length along ${t}_{2g}$, but due to uneven filling of electron in ${e}_{g}$ subset, either octahedral will be elongated or compressed.

Hence,$\left(\mathrm{Cu}{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{6}\right){\mathrm{SO}}_{4}$maximum structural distortion

Synergic bonding involves transference of electrons from ligands to metal. The transference of electrons takes place from filled metal orbitals to anti-bonding orbitals of ligands. It is a bond between a carbonyl group acting as a ligand and a metal. Synergic bonding means self strengthening bond. More the number of d electrons on the central metal ion more the synergic bonding. In metal carbonyls' oxidation state of the metal is zero.

All of these compounds can show synergic bonding.
